html:
The New Kingdom was ancient Egypt's age of empire, from about 1550 to 1069 BCE, when the pharaohs of the Eighteenth to Twentieth Dynasties ruled from Nubia to Syria. It was the richest and most powerful time in Egyptian history.

It began with war. Ahmose I, a king from Thebes, drove the Hyksos out of the delta and reunited the country. His successors built a standing army with horse-drawn chariots and pushed outward: south into Nubia, which they conquered for its gold, and north into Canaan and Syria.

Famous rulers:

  • Hatshepsut, a woman who ruled as king and sent a trading fleet to Punt.
  • Thutmose III, who won the largest empire, through some seventeen campaigns in the Levant.
  • Akhenaten, who tried to replace the old gods with the worship of the sun disc, the Aten.
  • Tutankhamun, who restored the old religion and died young.
  • Ramesses II, who fought the Hittites at Kadesh and built the temples of Abu Simbel.

Kings were buried in rock-cut tombs in the Valley of the Kings at Thebes, and the temple of Amun at Karnak grew into one of the largest religious buildings ever made.

Around 1177 BCE Ramesses III beat back the Sea Peoples, but Egypt lost its Asian empire in the crisis that ended the Bronze Age. Later kings grew weaker, tomb robbing spread, and the priests of Amun at Thebes became rulers in their own right. By 1069 BCE the country was split, and the Third Intermediate Period began.
sum: The New Kingdom was ancient Egypt's age of empire, from about 1550 to 1069 BCE, when the pharaohs of the Eighteenth to Twentieth Dynasties ruled from Nubia to Syria. It was the richest and most powerful time in Egyptian history.
